eval_texts: The case originated in an application (no. 5989/03) lodged with the Court under Article 34 of the Convention for the Protection of Human Rights and Fundamental Freedoms. The applicant alleged that civil proceedings initiated by her had not been determined within a reasonable time. The Government were represented by their Agent, Mrs [PERSON] of the Ministry of Justice. The application was originally allocated to the First Section of the Court. The case was assigned to the newly constituted Fifth Section (Rule 25 § 5 and Rule 52 § 1 of the Rules of Court) The circumstances of the case were as follows: The applicant suffered severe problems with her jaw, resulting in her being able to open her mouth only 5 millimetres. The applicant claimed compensation for her medical costs, loss of working capacity and disablement. The case was re-submitted to the Medico‑Legal Council with further questions. The National Board of Health issued their opinion on [DATE_TIME]. The applicant was awarded anticipatory pension. The applicant appealed against the decision of the National Patients' Complaints Board, which found against the applicant. The application was dismissed on appeal and the case was adjourned until later in the year. The matter was referred to the City Court of Hillerød (Retten i Hilleraod) for further proceedings. The Medico-Legal Council submitted their opinion. The Medical Officer of Health of Frederiksborg Amt (Retslægerådet) submitted their recommendation. The City Court requested that the parties inform it of what was holding up the case, and indicated that it would be set down for trial should the parties not reply within [DATE_TIME]. The parties informed the City Court of their intentions anew to put questions before the Medico-Legal Council and the National Board of Health. The City Court ordered that the applicant's counsel file a pleading within DATE TIME, following which the court ordered the applicant to change his writ and only invoke product liability. The applicant's prosecution was eventually granted a postponement to submit his pleading, and a court hearing was held on [Date_TIME. The applicant's pension case file was consulted, and the case was brought before a dental consultant and a neurological specialist of the National Board of Industrial Injuries. The applicant's claim amounted to 908,996 Danish kroner (DKK) The parties' counsel agreed to obtain the applicant's patient files from three hospitals and to draft questions to the Medico-Legal Council, when the material was available. The parties requested an adjournment of the proceedings pending their drafting those questions. The hearing was re-scheduled for [DATE_TIME]. Counsel was also granted an extension of the time-limit to submit the final claim. The applicant's amended claim amounted to DKK 908,583 in compensation. She waived her request for having part of the case heard separately in order to await the ruling of the European Court of Justice. The City Court found that a basis of liability existed, and that compensation could be granted for the pain, but not for the applicant's reduced ability to open her mouth. The trial was held on [DATE_TIME] and the case was set down for judgment. The case will now be heard in the Supreme Court (Højesteret) in the case of Frederiksborg v. Sønderborg. By judgment the City Court found for the applicant, who was granted compensation in the amount of DKK 676,900. The defendant was ordered to pay the applicant's costs and expenses. The case was appealed against the judgment to the High Court of Eastern Denmark. The Medico-Legal Council issued their opinion after four deliberating experts had had the case submitted three times. The High Court granted a request to put supplementary questions to the Medico‑Legal Council. A Supreme Court judgment printed in the Weekly Law Review (Ugeskrift for [PERSON]), [DATE_TIME], page 2390, concerned a patient who died due to medical malpractice. Without pursuing the case before any administrative bodies, the surviving spouse brought an action directly before the City Court, claiming compensation for pain and suffering. Three deliberating experts had assessed the case. The parties had entered a friendly settlement according to which [LOCATION] was to pay the applicant DKK 477,503 plus VAT in compensation. The High Court ordered that each party should pay their own costs and expenses.
